texts.preamble: Kantibhai Motibhai Limbachiya vs Dineshchandra Chunilal Gandhi & ... on 29 March, 2016 Author: K.J.Thaker Bench: K.J.Thaker R/Cr.A/267/1998 Judgment In The High Court Of Gujarat At Ahmedabad Criminal Appeal No. 267 of 1998 For Approval And Signature: Honourable Mr.Justice K.J.Thaker ========================================================== 1
texts.facts: By way of this appeal, the appellant has felt aggrieved as the accused were acquitted by the learned Magistrate for the offence under section 7(1) of the Food Adulteration Act vide judgment and order dated 20.3.1997 in Criminal Case No.9939 of 1986. 2. Before adverting to the facts, it was stated by Mr. Patel that identical matters of the same district were disposed of vide judgment dated 29.12.2008, and therefore, he requested that this matter should also meet the same fate. However, those matter were disposed of on 29.12.2008.
texts.arguments: Marshal learned counsel appearing for the respondents submitted that though the matters were remanded, and in most of the matters acquittal has been recorded by the learned trial court, which fact is not disputed by Mr. Patel. It is submitted by the learned advocate for the appellant that on the factual scenario learned trial Judge could not have acquitted the accused, who were facing grave charges of committing adulteration. The grounds urged are that the learned Magistrate ought to have held that the sample itself was adulterated. Just because the sample was taken in presence of one panch, it was not vitiate the entire trial. On the factual scenario, it is submitted by Mr. Marshal learned counsel for the respondents that the learned trial Judge has given elaborate reasons and the certificate is given after 8 days which is issued on 21.2.1986.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Marshal learned counsel appearing for the respondents submitted that though the matters were remanded, and in most of the matters acquittal has been recorded by the learned trial court, which fact is not disputed by Mr. Patel.
